turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil asked Sandip if he was truly so blind to the reality of the situation, and if he was aware of the consequences of his actions.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip told Nikhil that he was not afraid of Nikhil's empty threats and that he would rather have a debate on the matter than be intimidated by Nikhil's pretensions to authority.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil told Sandip that he was astonished that Sandip did not comprehend the gravity of the situation, and that his refusal to listen to reason was a grave mistake.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip chuckled and said, 'You're so good at playing the role of the brave zamindar, Nikhil, but I'm afraid you're not fooling anyone, least of all me.'

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil insisted that Sandip's flippant attitude was a threat to the very stability of the region, and that he would no longer engage in pointless banter.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip laughed and said, 'You're so fixated on your own importance, Nikhil, that you're forgetting that the only thing in danger here is your own dignity.'

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil said that he would no longer stand idly by while Sandip's reckless behavior put the entire community at risk.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he was starting to feel a little too powerful for his own good, and if his newfound sense of importance was worth risking a few bruised egos.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil warned Sandip that his continued disregard for the situation would be seen as a sign of weakness, and that the community would suffer the consequences.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip told Nikhil that his dire warnings were as predictable as a sunrise, and that he was starting to sound like a broken record.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil pointed out that Sandip's flippant attitude was a clear indication of his lack of understanding of the situation and his responsibility to the community.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip retorted that Nikhil was only warning him because he wanted to be the one to play the hero, saving the community from his supposedly reckless behavior.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil insisted that he would not be swayed by Sandip's personal opinions and would continue to warn him about the impending danger, no matter how uncomfortable it was.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip laughed, a hint of mockery in his tone, and said, 'Oh, Nikhil, always so dramatic and yet so predictable. Can't you see I'm busy writing a poem about the impending doom you keep warning me about?'

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil told Sandip that his flippant behavior was a dereliction of his duty as a member of this community, and that he would not tolerate such levity in the face of real danger.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip said with a chuckle, 'You're so fond of being the doomsday prophet, Nikhil. Perhaps you should write a poem about it -

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala asked in a calm, measured tone, 'Nikhil, what makes you so certain of these attacks? Is there any concrete evidence to support your claims?'

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil insisted that the recent tensions between the Hindus and Mussulmans in the neighboring village were a clear indication of the impending danger, and that he would not be deterred by Sandip's skepticism.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip sneered at Nikhil's warnings, 'And what makes you think I'm not prepared for these so-called attacks, Nikhil? I've been preparing my men for weeks, and we'll be ready to defend our land, should the need arise.'

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil firmly declared that being prepared was not the same as being vigilant, and that he would not stand idly by while the community was put at risk.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Bimala where she would go, addressing her as the Queen.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he kept Browning among his books, reminding him of a contest they had over translating lines from Browning, and inquiring if Nikhil remembered it.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Nikhil and Bimala that he had managed to translate the lines into Bengali, but the result was unlikely to be well-received, and that he had once thought he was on the verge of becoming a poet, but Providence had intervened to prevent it, and he recalled old Dakshina's poetry.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Bimala that it was pointless to search the bookshelves, as Nikhil no longer read poetry since his marriage, but that he, Sandip, was about to be afflicted with the 'fever fit of poesy' again.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil warned Sandip that he had come to give him a warning.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he was warning him about the 'fever fit of poesy'.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that for some time, Mahomedan preachers had been stirring up the local Mussulmans, who were angry with Sandip and might attack him at any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he had come to advise him to flee.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that he had come to give him information, not advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Nikhil that if the estates were his, a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for him, and that Nikhil should intimidate the preachers instead of frightening him, and that Nikhil's weakness was also affecting his neighbouring zamindars.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that he had not offered him advice, and that he wished Sandip would refrain from giving him his advice, as it was useless, and that there was another thing he wanted to tell Sandip, namely that Sandip and his followers had been secretly oppressing Nikhil's tenantry, and that he could no longer allow that, so he must ask Sandip to leave his territory.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he was threatening him with fear of the Mussulmans, or if there was another fear he had to threaten him with.
